name: Yann-Eric Hofmann
role: Federal Judge, Second Criminal Law Division, Federal Supreme Court of Switzerland (juge fédéral à la deuxième Cour de droit pénal)
party: Le Centre (Die Mitte), as published by the Federal Supreme Court
bio: Yann-Eric Hofmann, born in Fribourg in 1978, is a judge of the Federal Supreme Court of Switzerland and, as of October 2026, sits in its Second Criminal Law Division. He was elected a federal judge by the United Federal Assembly on 15 March 2023, on a party's proposal, as Swiss federal judges are; the Court lists his party as Le Centre (The Centre). A law graduate of the University of Fribourg, he was a clerk at the Federal Administrative Court and the Fribourg Cantonal Court, a legal adviser at the Federal Office for Spatial Development (2013–2019), a deputy and then ordinary judge of the Fribourg Cantonal Court (2014–2023) and a deputy judge of the Federal Supreme Court (2019–2023); since February 2025 he has co-chaired the steering committee of Justitia 4.0, the Swiss judiciary's digitalisation project. In September 2023 he was a member of the panel in cases 7B_15/2021 and 7B_16/2021, whose statement that a lower court could take into account the relatively short duration of a rape in sentencing was disavowed by the Court in a separate 2024 judgment; the collegial judgment does not identify the author of that passage or how each judge voted.
